name: volume_clock_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Traditional 1-min time bars treat all minutes equally, but market information arrival is uneven. Volume-clock bars (bars formed after every N shares traded) normalize for information flow, making technical signals more stationary. By computing RSI and Bollinger Bands on volume-clock bars instead of time bars, overbought/oversold signals become more reliable. The inefficiency exists because: (1) virtually all Indian retail traders use time-based charts exclusively, (2) volume-clock bar construction requires custom infrastructure, and (3) the resulting signals fire at irregular times, making manual trading impractical. In Indian markets where volume concentrates in the first and last hour, volume bars capture 60%+ of the daily signal in these windows, ignoring the noisy midday.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹50 crore, average daily volume > 1M shares

other: cumulative volume counter for volume-clock bar construction

entry.entry_price: limit at vol_bar_close on signal bar

exit.time_stop: exit after 10 volume-clock bars (~10-15 min in active periods)

filters.vix_filter: widen BB to 2.5 std when India_VIX > 20
filters.time_filter: no trades in first 5 min or last 10 min of session
filters.volume_filter: skip if volume-clock bar takes > 5 min to form (illiquid period)
filters.trend_filter: align with 20-period SMA direction on volume-clock bars
filters.spread_filter: skip if current bid-ask spread > 5 bps
filters.event_filter: no filter (volume bars naturally adapt to event-driven volume)
other_filters: skip if < 50 volume bars formed so far today (insufficient data)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — volume-clock bar infrastructure is a barrier to entry. Academic awareness is growing (Lopez de Prado) but practical adoption in Indian retail is still negligible.

weaknesses: Volume-clock bars fire rapidly during open/close auctions, potentially generating many signals in quick succession when slippage is worst.
The vol_bar_size parameter (ADV/300) is arbitrary and may need daily recalibration; stocks with changing liquidity profiles will produce inconsistent signals.
Backtesting volume-clock strategies is significantly harder than time-bar strategies, making it difficult to validate edge before live deployment.
prior_art: Lopez de Prado (2018) 'Advances in Financial Machine Learning' ch. 2 on volume, dollar, and tick bars. Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara (2012) on information-driven bars. Mandelbrot (1963) on subordinated time processes.
notes: Implementation requires a custom bar builder that accumulates volume from 1-min OHLCV and forms a new bar when cumulative volume exceeds vol_bar_size. All indicators must be recomputed on each new volume bar, not on each 1-min bar.
